headers.content-type: The type of the body, and its character set for a text.
headers.content-length: The size of the body, in bytes.
headers.content-encoding: The compression applied to the body, to undo before reading it.
headers.content-language: The language of the audience the content is meant for.
headers.content-disposition: Whether to show the body or download it, and under which name.
headers.content-location: The URL of the representation sent, when it differs from the one asked for.
headers.transfer-encoding: How the body is framed for transport in HTTP/1.1: chunked when its size is not known in advance.
headers.accept: The content types the client accepts, in order of preference.
headers.accept-encoding: The compressions the client can undo.
headers.vary: The request headers the response depends on: a cache keeps one copy per value.
headers.cache-control: The caching rules: who may keep the response, and for how long.
headers.expires: The date the response goes stale; Cache-Control max-age wins over it.
headers.age: How many seconds the response has spent in a cache.
headers.etag: The fingerprint of this version of the resource, to send back in If-None-Match or If-Match.
headers.last-modified: When the resource was last modified.
headers.if-none-match: The body only if the ETag changed, otherwise a 304.
headers.if-modified-since: The body only if it changed since that date, otherwise a 304.
headers.if-match: Apply the change only if the ETag still matches, otherwise a 412.
headers.if-unmodified-since: Apply the change only if nothing changed since that date, otherwise a 412.
headers.range: Only part of the resource is asked for.
headers.accept-ranges: The server accepts partial requests, in this unit.
headers.content-range: Which part of the resource the body holds, and its total size.
headers.if-range: The range only if the resource has not changed, otherwise the whole body.
headers.authorization: The client's credentials: a token, or Basic followed by name:password in Base64.
headers.www-authenticate: How to authenticate, sent with a 401.
headers.proxy-authorization: The credentials meant for the proxy.
headers.proxy-authenticate: How to authenticate with the proxy, sent with a 407.
headers.cookie: The cookies the browser sends back to the site.
headers.set-cookie: Sets a cookie, with its attributes.
headers.httponly: A Set-Cookie attribute: the cookie is hidden from JavaScript, so out of an injected script's reach.
headers.secure: A Set-Cookie attribute: the cookie only travels over HTTPS.
headers.samesite: A Set-Cookie attribute: Strict, Lax or None decide whether the cookie goes with a request coming from another site; the defence against CSRF.
headers.domain: A Set-Cookie attribute: extends it to the subdomains; without it, the cookie stays with the exact host.
headers.path: A Set-Cookie attribute: the paths under which the cookie is sent.
headers.max-age: A Set-Cookie attribute: its lifetime in seconds; without it or Expires, the cookie dies with the session.
headers.__host-: A name prefix: the browser accepts the cookie only if it is Secure, without Domain and on Path=/.
headers.strict-transport-security: Makes the browser use only HTTPS for this site for max-age seconds.
headers.content-security-policy: Where the page may load scripts, styles, images and frames from; the main defence against XSS.
headers.content-security-policy-report-only: The same policy, reported without being enforced: to try it first.
headers.x-content-type-options: Forbids the browser from guessing a type other than Content-Type.
headers.x-frame-options: Forbids showing the page in another site's frame; CSP's frame-ancestors replaces it.
headers.referrer-policy: What Referer reveals of the page when leaving it.
headers.permissions-policy: The browser features the page and its frames may use.
headers.cross-origin-opener-policy: Isolates the window from those another site opens, or that opened it.
headers.cross-origin-embedder-policy: Accepts only the cross-origin resources that allow it; with COOP, the isolation that unlocks SharedArrayBuffer.
headers.cross-origin-resource-policy: The sites that may embed this resource.
headers.clear-site-data: Clears the site's cache, cookies or storage in the browser, on logout for instance.
headers.x-xss-protection: Old browsers' XSS filter: set it to 0 or leave it out, CSP replaces it.
headers.origin: Where the request comes from: scheme, host and port, no path.
headers.access-control-allow-origin: The origin allowed to read the response, or * for all, without credentials.
headers.access-control-allow-credentials: The response may be read even when the request carries cookies or authentication.
headers.access-control-allow-methods: The methods allowed, in answer to a preflight (OPTIONS).
headers.access-control-allow-headers: The headers the request may carry.
headers.access-control-expose-headers: The response headers JavaScript may read, beyond the simplest ones.
headers.access-control-max-age: How many seconds to keep the answer to the preflight.
headers.access-control-request-method: In the preflight: the method that will follow.
headers.access-control-request-headers: In the preflight: the headers that will follow.
headers.host: The host name and port aimed at; required in HTTP/1.1.
headers.connection: Keep the connection open or close it, and the headers meant for this hop alone.
headers.upgrade: Switch to another protocol on the same connection.
headers.forwarded: The original client as a proxy saw it: its address, the protocol, the host; the standard form of X-Forwarded-*.
headers.x-forwarded-for: The client's address, then each proxy's; forgeable, to trust only from a trusted proxy.
headers.x-forwarded-proto: The protocol the client used in front of the proxy.
headers.x-forwarded-host: The host the client asked for in front of the proxy.
headers.x-request-id: One id per request, to follow it through every service's logs.
headers.user-agent: The client's software, and often its platform.
headers.referer: The page the request comes from; the misspelling is the standard's.
headers.expect: Wait for a 100 before sending the body.
headers.sec-fetch-site: Set by the browser: whether the request comes from the same site or another; enough to refuse CSRF on the server.
headers.location: Where to go: the target of a redirect, or the resource a 201 created.
headers.retry-after: When to try again, in seconds or as a date: with a 429 or a 503.
headers.allow: The methods the resource accepts, with a 405.
headers.server: The server's software; a version shown informs an attacker.
headers.link: Links to other resources: preloading, pagination, canonical URL.
headers.alt-svc: The same service elsewhere or otherwise; how a browser finds HTTP/3.
headers.server-timing: Where the server spent its time, shown in the browser's dev tools.
